chunks: "Too many vias hurts in four ways.
First, space: every through via puts a pad on every layer and cuts a hole in every plane, so a few thousand of them take a real chunk of routing area and make it harder to route.

Second, signal and plane integrity: the antipads can merge and perforate the reference planes, which makes return currents detour, raises plane impedance, and increases crosstalk and EMI; and each signal via is its own small inductive bump.
Third, cost and yield: the fab has to drill every hole, bits wear out, and more holes means more chances for a defect.
Fourth, reliability: every barrel is a possible fatigue crack or plating void site, and a board with many holes is slightly weaker mechanically.

So I'd keep the count down by routing on a layer when I can, using blind or microvias where density needs it, and when I do need a lot of vias, staggering them so the antipads don't line up into a slot."
